raw_case_text: A 1-year old female child was referred to us with fever of 1-week duration and altered sensorium. She was initially assessed by the emergency paediatrician. She was drowsy with a GCS of 9/15. A CT scan was advised which revealed bilateral cerebellar infarcts and patchy hypodensities in the left middle cerebral artery territory [Figures 6 and 7]. There was dilatation of the ventricles suggestive of obstructive hydrocephalus. She was referred to us for urgent intervention. After evaluating her clinically, placement of external ventricular drain was planned as an emergency measure to relieve the obstructive hydrocephalus. Preoperative investigations revealed she had low platelet count(30,000/mm3) and also showed positive reaction to dengue NS1 antigen. Her INR was 1.4 and APTT was 45 s. Multiple platelet transfusions were given with a modest rise in platelet counts to 50,000/mm3. An EVD was placed over the right Kocher's point to relieve the hydrocephalus after which the child became conscious to a GCS of 11/15. She started to localize for pain. After 1 week of placing the EVD, we were planning to convert it into a permanent ventriculoperitoneal shunt but her platelet counts never reached a crescendo to ensure a safe neurosurgical intervention. After 10 days when her platelets improved to 95,000/mm3, the EVD was clamped overnight. As there was no deterioration in her consciousness, the EVD was removed after draining a moderate amount of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). Unfortunately, within 15 min of this, there was sudden worsening of her neurological status to decerebrate posturing with anisocoria. The EVD was immediately reinserted along the previous track. An urgent CT scan was taken which revealed a large intracerebral hematoma in the opposite cerebral hemisphere [Figure 8]. She went into profound hypotension and her pupils became nonreactive following this. She was started on hemodynamic supports with dual vasopressors but succumbed to a cardiac arrest on the next day.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 1-year-old female presenting with a 1-week history of fever, drowsiness, and altered sensorium.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: A 1-year-old female presented with a 1-week history of fever and progressive alteration of sensorium. Initial evaluation demonstrated acute drowsiness and obstructive hydrocephalus due to cerebellar strokes, necessitating emergent external ventricular drain (EVD) placement. Following 10 days of stabilization, EVD was removed; however, 15 minutes post-removal she suffered acute neurological collapse with decerebrate posturing and anisocoria due to a massive contralateral intracerebral hematoma.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for fever, drowsiness, and loss of consciousness. Other systems untestable due to age and sensorium. Medications: blood product transfusions, vasopressors. Allergies: null.

objective.physical_examination: Drowsy on presentation with Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score 9/15. Post-initial EVD placement: GCS improved to 11/15 with pain localization. Terminal deterioration: Decerebrate posturing, anisocoria progressing to bilaterally fixed and dilated nonreactive pupils, and profound hemodynamic shock.
objective.routine_investigations: Platelet count: 30,000/mm3 on presentation, rising to 50,000/mm3 after multiple platelet transfusions, and reaching 95,000/mm3 on day 10. Coagulation: INR 1.4, aPTT 45 sec.
objective.advanced_workup: Brain CT (initial): Bilateral cerebellar infarcts and patchy hypodensities in the left middle cerebral artery territory with ventricular dilatation indicative of obstructive hydrocephalus. Brain CT (post-decompensation): Large acute intracerebral hematoma in the contralateral cerebral hemisphere. Invasive procedure: Right Kocher's point external ventricular drain (EVD) placement and subsequent emergency reinsertion.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Severe dengue infection presenting with ischemic cerebral/cerebellar infarctions and acute hydrocephalus, complicated by fatal secondary contralateral intracerebral hemorrhage following external ventricular drain removal. Diagnostic confirmation: Positive dengue virus nonstructural protein 1 (NS1) antigen.
Plan & Outcome: Emergency right frontal EVD placement and multiple platelet transfusions to correct severe thrombocytopenia. Following sudden post-drain removal neurological deterioration, emergency EVD reinsertion and initiation of dual inotropic/vasopressor support were instituted. The patient developed refractory hemodynamic collapse and suffered a fatal cardiac arrest on the next day.
